verdicts.reason: Both separate the beige circle from the book, so it ends up as a stray blob cut off at the right edge, and both put the book before the headline, reversing the original reading order. A pushes the book further left, which leaves less dead space on the left (about 130px against about 155px in B) and balances the strip slightly better.

These are almost pixel-identical. Both keep the original order (headline, then book on the right) and the text is readable, but both leave about 160px of empty space on the left and keep the beige circle as a cropped blob at the right edge, detached from the book it used to frame.

A keeps the circle behind the book, but it shrinks the body copy until it can't be read, wraps the headline onto two lines in a 90px banner, and crams everything into the middle with large empty strips on both sides. B has the usual flaws (book before headline, circle orphaned at the right edge) but its headline and body text are readable and laid out left to right.

Same layout in both: book on the left, single-line headline, circle orphaned and cropped at the right, and the reading order reversed from the original. B shifts the whole group further right, adding empty space on the left and squeezing the gap before the circle, so A is marginally better balanced.
